issue: dʰéh₁mn̥ 'house, home' (lexicon second sense); ugʷsénh₁e is the lexicon's ox stem
h₂éwh₂os 'maternal uncle' is the lexicon's second sense
réh₁toh₂ is 'meet' (pie-lex-reh1tt), English 'find' threads: stretched sense
tríh₂-kʷe usmń̥bʰis: 'garment' is INS.PL, but 'left three garments' needs ACC.PL wésmn̥h₂ (as in the later kʷíh₁ tríh₂ wésmn̥h₂); numeral and noun disagree in case
yéh₁ni is LOC of 'year' (pie-lex-yoh1r); English 'at the harvest' stretches the sense
stégesh₂ is NOM/ACC PL 'roofs'; English 'the roof split' is singular (later stégos SG): number changes the meaning
gʰrómōd 'roar' rendered 'thunder': stretched sense; pr̥h₂wós masc with 'cow' follows lexicon gender m of gʷṓws

PIE 'swésores-kʷe toy h₁wédm̥nih₁ bʰágonti' (and your sisters receive bride-prices) has no English ('You shall receive one, son,' then 'What is a dowry?'); also h₁wédmn̥ is 'bride price', English 'dowry' (minor)
linékʷti … ne gʷm̥yéti: pro-drop subject reads as the giver (previous subject), English means the guest; 'But' not in PIE
túH moy ḱéywōm: ḱéywōm is GEN.PL; the predicate 'dear' needs NOM.SG ḱéywos (or fem.)
'my husband is cooking a ram': pótim is ACC.SG, subject needs NOM pótis; and 'Bring them' and 'my husband is cooking' are run into one clause sequence without the sentence break the English has
